skill.name: Comma after an opening phrase ("At dawn, ...")
skill.why: The comma shows readers where the opening ends and the main part begins.
skill.how: Starts with a when, where or how phrase? Put the comma after the whole phrase.

steps.say: Tully here! Some sentences start by telling you when something happened.

show.nudge: The yeti is who did something. Which part tells you when?
Yawned is what the yeti did. Which part tells you when?

steps.ask: Tap the part that tells you when.
steps.win: Yes! At dawn tells you when. It has no doer of its own. It is an opening phrase.

steps.say: Some openers are long. The comma goes after the whole opener, not inside it.

show.nudge: At the top of... what? The where part isn't finished yet. Read on.
Stopped is what we did. Has the where part already finished?

steps.win: Yes! 'At the top of the hill' is the whole where part. The comma goes right after it.

steps.say: Some openers tell you how something happened.

show.nudge: The yeti is who did something. Which part tells you how?
That is what the yeti did. Which part tells you how?

steps.ask: Tap the opening phrase. This one tells you how.
steps.win: Yes! It tells you how. Openers that start with words like with, at or in are prepositional phrases.

steps.say: Watch out! Leave the comma out, and this sounds like someone ate the yeti.

show.nudge: After what? The when part isn't finished yet.
Now it says 'After eating the yeti'. Yikes! Where does the when part really end?
That comma would split the yeti from what it did. Where does the when part end?

steps.ask: Tap the word the comma goes after, so the yeti is safe.
steps.win: Phew! After eating, the yeti had a nap. Now the yeti is the one eating.

steps.say: Your turn. I'm in this one! Find the end of the whole when part.

show.nudge: During what? The when part has only just started.
The last minute of... what? Keep reading to the end of the when part.
That comma would split Tully from what she did. Where does the when part finish?

steps.ask: Tap the word the comma goes after.
steps.win: Yes! 'During the last minute of the game' is the whole opener. Comma, then the main part.

terms.means: Starts the sentence and tells when, where or how. It has no doer.
Who did what. It makes sense on its own.

card.test: Find where the whole when, where or how opener ends. Put the comma there.
